task.situation: Your neighbor, Mr. Daniel Ortiz, kindly watered your plants and collected your mail while you were away for a week. You want to thank him and do something nice for him in return.
task.recipient: Mr. Daniel Ortiz, your next-door neighbor
requirements: Thank him for his help while you were away.
Tell him about something you did on your trip.
Invite him to have dinner with you.

task.situation: You recently joined the campus photography club. The club leader asked new members to share what kind of photos they like to take so that she can plan the first outing.
task.recipient: Ms. Hannah Lee, the president of the campus photography club
requirements: Introduce yourself briefly.
Describe the kind of photos you enjoy taking.
Suggest a place the club could visit for its first outing.

task.situation: You borrowed a book from your instructor to help with a class project. Unfortunately, you spilled coffee on the cover, and now it is stained.
task.recipient: Dr. Samuel Price, your history instructor
requirements: Explain what happened to the book.
Apologize for the damage.
Offer a way to make up for it.

task.situation: You signed up for a weekend cooking class at a community center. When you arrived, the class had been moved to another building, but no one had told the students, and you missed the first hour.
task.recipient: Mr. Victor Haines, the program manager at the community center
requirements: Describe what happened when you arrived.
Explain how the change affected you.
Suggest how the center could inform students about changes in the future.

task.situation: Your university is planning to update the student lounge in your dormitory and has asked residents for ideas. You use the lounge often and have noticed several things that could be improved.
task.recipient: Ms. Rachel Kim, the housing services coordinator
requirements: Explain how you currently use the lounge.
Describe one problem with the lounge.
Recommend a specific improvement and explain why it would help.

task.situation: A friend from another city is planning to visit your town next month and has asked for your advice. You know the area well and want to help your friend make the most of the trip.
task.recipient: Leo Martins, a friend who is planning to visit
requirements: Recommend a place your friend should visit.
Explain the best way to get around town.
Suggest something you could do together during the visit.

task.situation: You work part-time at the campus bookstore. Your manager has just posted the schedule for next month, but you are scheduled to work on the same day as an important exam.
task.recipient: Ms. Olivia Grant, the manager of the campus bookstore
requirements: Explain the scheduling conflict.
Ask for a change to your schedule.
Offer a solution that would make the change easier for her.

task.situation: You are part of a four-person group working on a semester-long research project. One member has missed the last three meetings and has not finished his part, and the deadline is in two weeks.
task.recipient: Professor Alan Whitfield, the instructor of your sociology course
requirements: Describe the situation in your group.
Explain what your group has already tried to do about it.
Ask for advice on how to proceed fairly.

task.situation: Your town's public library is considering reducing its weekend hours to save money. The library director has asked community members to share their opinions before a final decision is made.
task.recipient: Ms. Teresa Vaughn, the director of the public library
requirements: Explain how you or others use the library on weekends.
Describe what might happen if the hours are reduced.
Propose another way the library could save money.

task.situation: You attended an academic conference that your department helped pay for. The department chair has asked you to report on the experience because she is deciding whether to fund more students next year.
task.recipient: Dr. Mei Lin Chen, the chair of your department
requirements: Describe one session that was especially valuable to you.
Explain how the experience will help your studies.
Recommend whether the department should fund more students, and explain why.

task.situation: Your English conversation partner, Ms. Julia Novak, has invited you to a small birthday party at her home this Saturday. You have already promised to help a friend move to a new apartment that day.
task.recipient: Ms. Julia Novak, your English conversation partner
requirements: Thank her for the invitation.
Explain why you cannot come.
Suggest another time to celebrate together.

task.situation: Your university is replacing printed course packets with digital readings to reduce costs. Many students in your program have told you they find it hard to concentrate and take notes when reading long texts on a screen.
task.recipient: Dr. Robert Hale, the director of your academic program
requirements: Describe the difficulties students are having with digital readings.
Explain why printed materials help some students learn.
Propose a compromise that would keep costs low.
